'''An Euclidean circle''' is a [[circle]] in the [[Euclidean space#Special_Euclidean_spaces|Euclidean plane]].

[[File:Circle-O-r.svg]]

== Formal definition ==

Let $\mathbb{E}^2$ be an [[Euclidean space#Special_Euclidean_spaces|Euclidean plane]].

$$
\text{Circle}(\vec{c},r)=\{\vec{x}\in\mathbb{E}^2:\|\vec{x}-\vec{c}\|=r,\,  r>0, \vec c \in \mathbb{E}^2\}
$$

== Cartesian coordinate description ==

Let $X,C \in \mathbb{E}^2$ be points in an [[Euclidean space#Special_Euclidean_spaces|Euclidean plane]].

Let
$$
\vec{x}=(x,y),\quad \vec{c}=(c_1,c_2)
$$

be their position vectors, then

$$
\vec{x}\in\text{Circle}(\vec{c},r)\iff (x-c_1)^2+(y-c_2)^2=r^2
$$
